name: Tsukumogami
description: Tsukumogami (付喪神) are a class of Japanese yokai in which household items and tools gain sentience and spiritual essence after approximately 100 years of existence; rooted in Shinto animism and Buddhist teachings, they can range from benign pranksters to vengeful spirits if discarded carelessly.

aliases.name: 付喪神
aliases.meaning: The kanji form: attached/grieving spirit of an object; read tsukumogami

aliases.name: 九十九神
aliases.meaning: Alternate kanji: ninety-nine spirits; emphasizes great age (100 years) as the threshold for animation

regions: Particularly associated with the Heian-period (794–1185 CE) court culture where many of the originating texts were composed
origin: Japan; the tsukumogami concept is specific to Japanese culture and is rooted in Shinto animism and Japanese Buddhist traditions.
